coordinate_evidence.statement: Centre of the site's PGDA 5 m/pixel LDEM tile, converted from south polar stereographic (lat_0 = -90, lon_0 = 0, k = 1, sphere R = 1737400 m, MOON_ME/DE421) to planetocentric latitude and east longitude. It is the centre of the mapped region, NOT a selected landing point.

sources.title: High-Resolution LOLA Topography for Lunar South Pole Sites (PGDA product 78)
Barker, M. K., et al. (2021). Improved LOLA elevation maps for south pole landing sites: error estimates and their impact on illumination conditions. Planetary and Space Science, 203, 105119.
Mazarico, E., et al. (2011). Illumination conditions of the lunar polar regions using LOLA topography. Icarus, 211(2), 1066-1081.
NASA (2022-08-19). NASA identifies candidate regions for landing next Americans on Moon (news release); NASA SVS 5013, Artemis III Landing Region Candidates.
sources.citation: the 13 Artemis III candidate regions; artemis_iii_2022_region mapping

coordinate_evidence.method: GeoTIFF ModelTiepoint/ModelPixelScale read with HTTP range requests; tile centre converted with the spherical polar stereographic inverse and cross-checked with PROJ via rasterio (exact agreement for Haworth, Site04, Site23).
assumptions: Each coordinate is a DEM tile centre, not a selected landing point.
limitations: Reference points are tile centres, not landing sites; the regions of interest are defined by the per-site ROI shapefiles (*_ROIs.tgz) on PGDA, not yet ingested.

The list of 13 Artemis III region names was confirmed from secondary coverage of NASA's 2022 release; nasa.gov is not reachable from the LUNARIS build environment. SVS 5013 (reachable) confirms the count and date but its text does not list names.
PGDA labels both Site11 and SL2 'de Gerlache rim'; which corresponds to NASA's 'de Gerlache Rim 1' vs 'Rim 2' is not established.
NASA revised the Artemis III candidate list after 2022; the 2022 list is used here and later revisions are not yet reflected.
